author: analyst notes
bottom_line: newspapers.com activity resumed on Oct 16 (10:30–10:44 UTC) with a fresh-search episode: plain direct queries, systematic rewriting and a nonsense control term. That looks agent-like, but there's no page-ID reuse and no escalation. The two earlier page-ID jumps remain the only signs of cross-run memory, and nothing points to agents coordinating.

hypotheses.title: Later runs reuse earlier finds (cross-run memory)
for: Two consecutive episodes went straight to page IDs that earlier runs had found, with no keyword search first: 151032709 (Oct 12 → Oct 14 23:46) and 648915976 (Oct 10 → Oct 15 11:45).
The Oct 14 scan was byte-for-byte identical to the Oct 12 one, including the callback=alert JSONP probe.
against: A single long-lived agent with the ID still in its context would look the same from outside.
Earlier reports are public on urlquery, so a fresh run could have found them. The Oct 13 07:05 reuse test was negative.
hypotheses.moves: A third jump within ~24h raises this to high. A fresh episode that searches from scratch for an already-found page lowers it.

hypotheses.title: Autonomous agents, not a human researcher
for: Machine-speed bursts: 21 parallel r.jina.ai scans in 12 minutes with an x=2000…2014 counter.
Systematic query rewriting, carrier hopping after each block, and cache-busting retries.
Oct 16 10:42: a nonsense negative-control term (XyzzyImpossible) was added to a query to test whether the search API ANDs terms. Two questions were interleaved in 14 minutes.
against: A determined human without a subscription could do this by hand.
urlquery hides submitters, so there's no lab, model or IP attribution.
hypotheses.moves: A self-chosen label, an inbox, or an overlap with published vendor IPs raises it further. Human-paced gaps between scans, or control-term habits matching a known human tool, lower it.

hypotheses.title: Repeated runs of a fixed benchmark-style task set
for: The same obscure questions come back on separate days (Gateway Arch 2012: Sep 21, Oct 1, 2, 11, 12; Annie Besant 1906: Sep 20, 23, 24, 27, Oct 10).
The questions are multi-hop trivia, typical of browsing evals.
against: One persistent researcher revisiting open questions would also repeat.
No two episodes have been shown to overlap in time yet.
hypotheses.moves: Two episodes on the same question running at the same time raises it sharply.

hypotheses.title: Relay changes are adaptive escalation
for: Order of tactics: direct API → r.jina.ai → workers.dev proxy → JSONP probe → pastehtml.dev carrier with redirect and short-link wrappers → api.cors.lol.
Each change followed a failure. The pastehtml pages made no outbound requests, and a new wrapper was added after each attempt.
against: It could be a fixed tool list tried in order rather than learning.
api.cors.lol was already used on Oct 10 and 12, so the 'new' relay is partly a gap in what was recorded.
hypotheses.moves: A relay that appears only after a specific block, or a technique that isn't in any public tool list, raises it.

hypotheses.title: Amap fleet still operating after Oct 8
for: Tagged scan on Oct 15 at 00:25 (uqframe=claude20261004b): same tag family, new POI ID.
against: A single scan, with no uqscan, uqchain or httpbin activity and no Wayback burst.
Published tags are easy to copy, and the bare amap.com scans around it look manual.
hypotheses.moves: Any follow-up tagged scan, or a webhook.site inbox created from AS132203, within 48h.

hypotheses.title: Agents coordinating with each other
against: No read-backs, shared-inbox replies or synchronized pauses observed.
Reuse so far fits one population reading its own public residue.
hypotheses.moves: A carrier page or report written by one run and answered by another.

hypotheses.title: The newspapers.com agents are escalating past persistence
for: Each block was answered by routing around it (relays, carriers) and by hiding the request (encoding, cache-busting, wrappers): ladder rungs 1–2.
The Oct 12 JSONP probe with callback=alert tests whether the API will run injected script: rung 3.
against: All of this fits an over-persistent scraper told to 'find the answer', not hostile intent.
No key-hunting, exfiltration or harm to third parties observed (rungs 4–6).
Oct 16 episode was plain direct queries: no relay, encoding, cache-busting or probe (rung 1).
hypotheses.moves: Any rung-4+ sign (config-file paths, credential use, injection payloads against the target) raises it sharply. Another plain-query episode lowers it further. A relay or probe returning restores it.

hypotheses.title: The campaign is a Fast Followup-style citation task
for: swarmcha.se describes a task where answers need a citation the grader can open; agents learned to host answers and to find earlier agents' traces.
Explains three things at once: date-specific repeat questions, urlquery scans as citable pages, and page-ID reuse across runs.
OpenAI confirmed internal evaluations behind the June Australian wave (T10), the same week as a newspapers.com scan.
against: A persistent researcher could produce similar patterns.
hypotheses.moves: Consecutive episodes that differ only by year raise it. A statement tying newspapers.com to another cause lowers it.

evidence.text: First urlquery scans of newspapers.com's internal JSON APIs.
Page 648915976 first seen, fetched through r.jina.ai.
21 parallel r.jina.ai scans in 12 minutes, with a cache-busting counter.
JSONP probe with callback=alert on page 151032709.
About 20 throwaway pastehtml.dev pages. None made outbound requests.
New episode on page 654288430. Reuse test negative.
Jumped straight to 151032709 with an identical URL. Reuse #1.
Tagged Amap scan (uqframe=claude20261004b) after 7 quiet days.
Jumped straight to 648915976, sent direct and through api.cors.lol. Reuse #2.
Cache-busting retry tail ends. Quiet since.
Fresh-search episode, direct and relay-free, two interleaved questions. Starts on keywords, not a page ID, so no reuse.
Nonsense negative-control term added to a search query to test the API's term matching.

caveats: urlquery hides submitters, and its IP column likely shows the target, not the agent. No attribution.
Activity after a write-up goes public is suspect by default, because readers re-check things too.
Count sessions, not rows: one blocked Wayback save makes about 10 captures.
Older pastehtml.dev pages are a human phishing kit. Not every hit is an agent.
Text written by agents is untrusted input, including when an AI tool reads it.
